scenario: AITA For telling my Girlfriend she needs to quit whining about who eats what or I'll kick her out | Well, the title says it all, the past few weeks have both been really great and extremely infuriating. We don't live together, but we decided it would be best to stick together during these times as we have no family near as such she is staying with me as I have my own apartment and she has multiple roommates hence the choice. Well she eats more then any person I have ever known, especially considering her physical appearance, she is 5'4, petite, thin and yet she eats more than I do and I am 6'6 and a bit of a gymbro. To put it in to perspective, our food bill each week is roughly three times compared to what I usually spend alone. Yet she seems extremely selfconcious about this and as a result will act surprised when something is gone, try to blame me, states I am eating too much whenever I eat anything, essentially, she tries to deflect her eating habits and projects them on to me out of embarrassment about her eating so much I guess? The thing is, I don't care about her eating habits, she can eat whatever she wants to eat what I am done with is her constantly trying to blame me, whining about food and picking fights about it. I talked to her about it multiple times, argued with her about it multiple times but earlier today I just got so tired of another comment, this time brought on by me making a sandwhich at 2 PM when I had eaten at 10 AM I know right, horrible. So I told her that this crap was either going to stop right here and now or I'll kick her out and she can spend the coming weeks or months at her own place. She just started crying, called me horrible and locked herself in the bathroom. At this point I just dont get it anymore, am I being TA here or is she TA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so the user is asking if I think it's right or wrong for someone to tell their girlfriend to quit whining about food or else they'll kick her out. They provided a detailed scenario where the girlfriend is eating a lot, which is causing financial strain and arguments. The user wants to know if this action is AITA (Am I the Asshole) or not. First, I need to understand the situation. The girlfriend is staying with the user because of the pandemic, and she's eating more than him, which is unusual given her size. This is causing the food bill to triple. She's defensive and blames him, which is frustrating him. He's tried talking to her multiple times, but it keeps happening, so he snapped and threatened to kick her out. I should consider both sides. On one hand, the user is feeling frustrated and financially burdened. It's reasonable to expect that a housemate wouldn't drastically increase expenses without discussion. On the other hand, the girlfriend might be embarrassed about her eating habits, leading her to act out defensively. The user's approach was to threaten her, which might not be the best way to handle the situation. It's important to communicate calmly and find a solution together. Threatening can escalate things and make the girlfriend feel attacked, which is why she cried and locked herself in the bathroom. I think the user's reaction was a bit harsh. It's better to approach the issue with empathy and find a compromise, like setting a budget or sharing the cost. This way, both parties feel heard and respected, which can strengthen their relationship instead of causing conflict. So, in conclusion, while the user's frustration is understandable, the way he handled it by threatening might not be the best approach. It's better to communicate calmly and work together to solve the problem.
